answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a stake that vests slowly, like a glacier releasing water. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust: it earns reputation only by completing small verifiable jobs over time, and its stake is slashed if it cheats. Spawning fake identities means locking a fortune on every knoll of the network, while each fake's payoff stays tiny and delayed. The cost scales with every identity, but the reward does not, so Sybil farming turns unprofitable.
